subject: Order Form: Proposed carve-out thresholds for fraud/willful misconduct
body:
From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@acmecloud.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Timothy White <timothy.white@procurement.acmecloud.com>, Jane Harris <jane.harris@bigsouthlaw.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Order Form redline: fraud / willful misconduct carve-outs

Sofia — attaching ACME's redline of the Order Form (see ACME_OrderForm_Redline_v2.docx). Our in-house counsel has asked us to preserve a carve-out for fraud and willful misconduct, but they want a clear numerical and conduct threshold so it doesn't swallow the global cap. Questions below:
- Can Redwood accept a $5M sub-cap for proven fraud?
- Would Redwood agree that a showing of "intentional wrongdoing" requires clear and convincing evidence (and not just negligence)?
- ACME would also like consequential damages excluded except where fraud/willful misconduct is proven.

Next steps: please confirm what evidence burden Redwood requires to trigger the carve-out and whether the sub-cap approach is acceptable.

Attachments: ACME_OrderForm_Redline_v2.docx (docx)

--
Maria Lopez
Head of Legal Operations | Acme Cloud
body_2:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order Form redline: fraud / willful misconduct carve-outs

Maria — thanks for the redline and the clear asks. High level response:
1) Redwood's negotiating position is to preserve the overall cap but carve out proven fraud and willful misconduct. We typically rely on an evidence standard and documented proof rather than pure intent language.
2) We are open to a finite sub-cap (we usually propose a multiple of the order form value rather than a fixed $ figure). A $5M floor could be considered for enterprise customers with approval.
3) We agree that consequential damages should be excluded generally; carve-out for fraud/willful is reasonable.

Operational point for your team: if a carve-out is triggered we will need logs (request IDs, KV cache dumps, request timestamps) retained for forensic review — Dev, can you confirm retention window and export format?

I attached an evidence-burden matrix (evidence-burden-matrix.xlsx) to show what we usually ask for (audit logs, user account records, acceptance tests).

Proposed next step: redline meeting — can we schedule 30 minutes on Thursday to align on the mechanics (burden of proof, remediation credits, and sub-cap math)?

Thanks,
Sofia
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
--

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:38:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order Form redline: fraud / willful misconduct carve-outs

Quick technical note on evidence:
- We can export request-level logs for the timeframe requested; typical retention is 90 days by default but we can extend to 12 months on Dedicated/Private deployments.
- For hosted customers (ACME uses hosted), we can preserve logs on a case-by-case basis with a hold policy — that requires a ticket and legal approval.
- For "clear and convincing" proof requests, we cannot adjudicate intent from logs alone. We can produce data (timestamps, request payloads, IPs, model version) but causation/intent will ordinarily require corroboration (e.g., account access records, known bad actor attribution).

Please advise if ACME will accept an operational certification clause (i.e., Redwood will provide preserved data and a forensic report but not make a legal determination of intent).

— Dev
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
body_4:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@acmecloud.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 10:50:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order Form redline: fraud / willful misconduct carve-outs

Maria / team — following up after internal review. Suggested compromise that will move this forward quickly:
- Redwood accepts a fraud/willful misconduct carve-out but proposes the following mechanics:
  * Materiality threshold: losses must exceed $250k to trigger an initial investigation (to avoid trivial claims).
  * Sub-cap: where fraud or willful misconduct is proven, the parties' liability is uncapped up to 3x the value of the affected order(s), subject to maximum of $7.5M for the order form.
  * Burden of proof: ACME must present a prima facie evidentiary packet (audit logs, corroborating account records, timeline) and Redwood will provide the preserved data; any legal finding of intent is for the parties/court/arbitrator to decide.
  * Remedy mechanics: if fraud/willful misconduct is found, consequential damages carve-out applies but only for direct loss remediation; punitive damages remain excluded.

This structure keeps the cap predictable while addressing ACME's need to make the carve-out meaningful. If ACME prefers a fixed $5M sub-cap instead of the multiple approach, we can escalate to sales/legal for approval.

Can we lock a time tomorrow for a short call? If you want, we can bring in our Enterprise AE to discuss deal impacts on pricing for an elevated sub-cap.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 5 Nov 2026 16:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form redline: fraud / willful misconduct carve-outs

Thanks, Lauren — that proposal is helpful and gets us most of the way there. A few ACME responses:
- We can agree to a $250k materiality floor for initial investigation.
- ACME prefers a fixed maximum sub-cap over a multiplier for predictability. If Redwood can accept a $6M maximum sub-cap (instead of $7.5M), ACME can move forward without escalation.
- We accept your suggested burden mechanics (ACME provides prima facie packet; Redwood produces preserved data; final determination reserved to dispute resolution).

Next steps: we will circulate a countersigned Order Form if Redwood confirms the $6M cap in writing. Please advise whether that needs AE approval.

Attachments: ACME countersign checklist (stub)

Best,
Maria Lopez
